title: The immune system
examples: What exactly are pathogens and how do they enter our bodies?
If I get a vaccine, what is actually happening in my immune system?
How does a fever help fight off an infection?

explain.say: Today we are learning about your amazing immune system. It is your body's natural defence team. It protects you from germs and sickness.
White blood cells are the main fighters of your immune system. They patrol your blood looking for invaders. They can engulf and destroy germs you pick up.
Antibodies are special Y-shaped proteins made by your body. They are designed to lock onto specific invaders. This marking helps other cells destroy them.
A fever is a natural defence mechanism your body uses. It raises your body temperature slightly. This higher heat makes it harder for some germs to survive.
When you get a cut, white blood cells rush to the area. They start to trap any germs that entered. Then, your body makes antibodies to target those specific germs.
In everyday life, when you get a vaccination, you are training your immune system. It teaches your body to recognize a specific germ safely. This way, it is ready if you meet the real germ later.

faq.q: How long do antibodies last in my body?
faq.a: Antibodies can last for a long time after exposure. Your body remembers the pattern of the germ. You might also hear it called 'memory cells'.
asks: Do I need to get boosters?

faq.q: Are white blood cells always present in my blood?
faq.a: Yes, white blood cells are always circulating in your blood. They are always ready to patrol for any sign of trouble. They are part of your bloodstream.
asks: Where do white blood cells live?
Do they only appear when I am sick?

faq.q: Is a high fever always good for me?
faq.a: A mild fever is usually a sign your body is fighting something off. However, a very high fever can sometimes cause other problems. Always listen to your doctor's advice.
asks: Should I take medicine for a fever?
What is the purpose of fever?

faq.q: What are pathogens, and are they all bad?
faq.a: Pathogens are just names for any germ that can cause disease. Some are harmless, but others can make us feel unwell. Bacteria and viruses are common types.
asks: What is the difference between a germ and a pathogen?
Are all bacteria bad for me?

faq.q: How does the immune system know which germ to fight?
faq.a: The immune system uses specialized receptors on its cells. These receptors recognize unique shapes on the surface of invaders. This recognition is very specific.
asks: Is the immune system like a lock and key?

facts: White blood cells are part of the circulatory system.
Antibodies have a specific shape to match a germ.
A fever increases body temperature to hinder pathogens.
Vaccines introduce weakened germs to train immunity.

quiz.say: Which component is responsible for recognizing and binding to specific foreign invaders?
quiz.why: Antibodies are shaped like keys that fit specific locks on germs.

wrong.1: White blood cells are the general fighters, not the specific binders.
wrong.2: Fever is a temperature change, not a physical binding molecule.
wrong.3: Pathogens are the invaders themselves, not the defense tool.

quiz.say: If your body temperature rises to 39 degrees Celsius, what is this most likely doing?

options.show: It means you are getting sick.
options.say: It means you are getting sick.

options.show: It is a sign of a broken bone.
options.say: It is a sign of a broken bone.

quiz.why: A fever is the body's way of making it harder for germs to grow.

wrong.0: It means you are fighting something, which is a good sign.
wrong.2: While it is high, the body raises it intentionally to help fight.
wrong.3: Fever relates to germs, not physical injury.

quiz.say: When a vaccine is given, what is the primary goal for your immune system?

options.show: To give you the actual germ.
options.say: To give you the actual germ.

options.show: To stop you from ever getting sick.
options.say: To stop you from ever getting sick.

quiz.why: The vaccine shows your body a safe sample so it remembers how to fight later.

wrong.1: Immunity from vaccines is long-lasting, not just temporary.
wrong.2: Vaccines use weakened parts, not the active, dangerous germ.
wrong.3: No medicine can guarantee you will never get sick from anything.
